Check Q3: 0.9995×0.999×0.9995×0.995 = compute: 0.9995×0.999=0.9985005; ×0.9995=0.9980010; ×0.995=0.99301... = 0.9930100. 99.30% ✓. Downtime 0.00699×720=5.03? Wait 0.00699×720 = 5.0328. Student wrote 3.5 hours — error! Actually 1−0.99301=0.00699; ×720=5.03. Student says 3.5 — arithmetic slip. (c): 0.999975 → 99.9975% but requested two decimals: 100.00%? Downtime 0.018 h ✓. So one arithmetic slip → Proficient (5-6), say 6? Method correct, one slip → 6.

Q4: circuit breaker states mixed up: Open = fail fast, Closed = normal. Student says "In the Open state calls pass through normally... breaker moves to Closed and calls fail immediately" — reversed. Explanation incorrect → Developing (1-2), say 2. Also no drawback/tuning? They mention threshold tuning. But explanation wrong → 2.

Q1: availability response measure "stay up most of the time" not measurable → Proficient 4.

Q2: excellent, two scenario-specific trade-offs, downside acknowledged → 5-6, say 6.

Q5: CAP explained incorrectly ("choose consistency and availability, give up partition tolerance" — P is not optional). Techniques: Redis cache named for menu; for payments no concrete technique named. → Proficient 3-4, say 3.

Q6: no negative consequence → Proficient 3-4, say 4? Context/Decision/Consequences present, positives only → 3.

C7: Q2 exceeds 150 words (~200). Q4 also long. References only one cited [1],[2] cited but [2] not in reference list. → Developing 2.
